findings.documented: The API key is supplied as the api_key query parameter, and protected requests use the documented token.
findings.actual: The live API requires X-API-Key and a Bearer access token. Login returns access_token and refresh_token.
findings.how_found: Sent the key using the documented query parameter which obviously did not work. The response indicated the correct headers.
findings.impact: Clients following the documented authentication flow cannot authenticate.

findings.documented: Login returns token and expires_in: 86400, with a full demo-user object.
findings.actual: Login returns access_token, refresh_token, refresh_url, token_type Bearer, expires_in 900, and a user object containing the email.
findings.how_found: Called the login endpoint and recorded the response.
findings.impact: A frontend relying on documented behavior will not be able to authenticate or maintain a session.

findings.actual: POST /auth/refresh accepts refresh_token and returns a refreshed access-token response.
findings.how_found: Called the refresh_url returned by login with the refresh token.
findings.impact: Clients have no idea of how to refresh their access tokens and will be forced to re-login every 15 minutes.

findings.documented: Logout invalidates the current token server side.
findings.actual: Logout returns ok true but says tokens are stateless. The token remains usable and must be discarded client side.
findings.how_found: Called logout and then used the same access token for another protected request.
findings.impact: Logout implementations must clear local cookies or storage; the API does not revoke the token.

findings.documented: Collections use page and limit, with a maximum limit of 200.
findings.actual: Collections use offset and limit. A requested limit of 200 is capped at 50, and responses include count, total, has_more, results, limit, and offset.
findings.how_found: Requested multiple collection pages and compared returned pagination metadata with the requested parameters.
findings.impact: Clients must advance offset using the returned batch and has_more instead of requesting page numbers.

findings.documented: total is exact and can be used to calculate all pages.
findings.actual: Complete traversal using has_more produced counts that can disagree with the reported total.
findings.how_found: Downloaded each collection to the end by following has_more and compared the resulting count with total.
findings.impact: Clients can not rely on total to calculate the number of pages, they must traverse the collection to the end.

findings.documented: The endpoint returns only active listings.
findings.actual: The endpoint returns both live and inactive records, is_live must be checked by the client.
findings.how_found: Retrieved all listing records and inspected their is_live values.
findings.impact: The frontend must not assume every returned listing is active.

findings.documented: furnishing, is_live, and project_id query parameters filter listings.
findings.actual: Those parameters were accepted but returned the same result totals and first records as the unfiltered request.
findings.how_found: Compared requests with each parameter against an otherwise identical unfiltered request.
findings.impact: The frontend must apply these filters locally.

findings.documented: A listing detail is available at the singular /v1/listing/{listing_id} path.
findings.how_found: Requested the documented route with a real listing ID.
findings.impact: Clients must use the plural detail route.

findings.documented: No plural listing detail route is documented.
findings.actual: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id} returns the listing detail object.
findings.how_found: Retried the documented detail request using the plural collection path.
findings.impact: This is the working route for listing detail pages.

findings.documented: The endpoint returns up to ten similar listings.
findings.how_found: Requested the documented similar-listings route with a real listing ID.
findings.impact: A similar-listings component must be derived locally or omitted.

findings.documented: Saved listings use GET, POST, and DELETE /v1/favourites routes.
findings.impact: Clients must use the live /v1/saved routes.

findings.actual: GET and POST /v1/saved work; POST accepts listing_id.
findings.how_found: Tested list and save operations with a real listing, then removed the test save.
findings.impact: This is the working saved-listing API.

findings.documented: No live delete route is documented under /v1/saved.
findings.how_found: Completed the save, list, and delete lifecycle.
findings.impact: The frontend can implement persistent per-user saved listings.

findings.documented: The endpoint returns pre-computed city analytics.
findings.how_found: Requested the documented analytics route after authentication.
findings.impact: Insights must be calculated from retrieved collections.

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are integer rupee values.
findings.actual: Project prices are decimal values with mixed lakh/crore encoding; for example P40001 has price_min 66.1 and price_max 1.95.
findings.how_found: Inspected all downloaded project prices and tested the unit hypothesis against impossible price_min > price_max pairs.
findings.impact: Project prices must be normalized before display and costliest-project calculations.

findings.documented: total_listings always agrees with currently available listings.
findings.actual: 119 projects have total_listings values different from the count of retrieved live listings linked to the project.
findings.how_found: Compared each project's total_listings with grouped live listing records.
findings.impact: Project listing counts should be labeled as API-reported values or reconciled client side.

findings.documented: Listing records describe ordinary real properties.
findings.actual: 45 records contain structurally impossible values, including negative prices, invalid floor relationships, impossible bedroom/property combinations, inverted areas, or invalid coordinates.
findings.how_found: Tested record-level invariants across the complete listing download.
findings.impact: These records if displayed would mislead users and analysts. The server should validate and reject them, or the frontend should filter them out.

findings.documented: Listing records are genuine property listings.
findings.actual: Nine positive-price records are strong fake-listing candidates because their prices are implausibly low for the dataset and they match the bait-listing pattern.
findings.how_found: Tested the low-price bait hypothesis against the complete listing dataset and reviewed the candidate records.
findings.impact: These records are excluded from the relevant average-price calculation and reported as fake candidates.
